full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 2-8-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Chattogram in Other Appeal No.406 of 2005 disallowing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 12-7-2005 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalkhali, Chattogram in Other Suit No.120 of 2002 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 7. Being aggrieved by above judgment and decree plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No. 406 of 2005 to the District Judge, Chattogram which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge who dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 8. Being aggrieved by above judgment and decree appellant as petitioner moved to this court and obtained this Rule. 

 9. Mr Md Aktaruzzaman learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the defendant admits his 6 signatures on the impugned bainapattra deed (Exhibit No. 1). But claims that he affixed those signature on blank stamp papers as a security of a loan of Taka 12,000 he obtained from the plaintiffs. But the defendant could not prove above claims by legal evidence. On the contrary PW 2 and 3 witnesses to above bainapattra have given consistent and manually supportive evidence in support of due execution of above deed. As PW 1 plaintiff has stated in his evidence that he got delivery of possession and erected fences around the disputed land. The plaintiff has succeeded to prove due execution of bainapattra dated 25-1-1998 and delivery of possession of the disputed land. But the learned Assistant Judge failed to consider above legal evidence on record and most illegally dismissed the suit. The learned Judge of the court of appeal below did not consider the materials on record independently and most illegally dismissed the Appeal and affirmed the flawed judgment and decree of the trail court in a slipshod manner which is not tenable in law. 

 11. Considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties and perused the impugned judgment and decree and other materials on record. 

 24. But the learned Assistant Judge deliberately overlooked the admissions made by DW 1 and most illegally dismissed the suit. The learned Additional District Judge instead of an independent assessment of total evidence on record reiterated the flawed findings of the trial court and most illegally dismissed the appeal and affirmed the erroneous judgment and decree of the trial court which is not tenable in law. 

 27. The impugned judgment and decree dated 2-8-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge in Other Appeal No. 406 of 2006 affirming the judgment and decree dated 14-7-2005 passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No.120 of 2002 is set-aside and above suit is decreed on contest against defendant No.1 and ex-parte against the rest without cost.
